## The assembly blocks' options, and four gates (TASKS item 17; decision items 107, 110, 111, 123; 2026-11-10)

- **What:** the design review's findings 2, 5, 6 (its last point) and 18 (its fifth), on branch `claude/funny-torvalds-9a28a0`. The contract is in `TASKS.md`, under item 17.
  - **The options.** An `asm!` block that declares `preserves_flags` promises the compiler that the status flags, the x87 status word and the exception flags of MXCSR are unchanged when it ends. 40 blocks declared it; 22 no longer do, and 18 still do. Only `options(…)` and the comments beside them changed: no instruction.

    | Blocks | Where | Why the promise was false, or not known to be true |
    |---|---|---|
    | 5 | `cpu.rs`: `load_page_tables`, `enable_global_pages`, `enable_simd` (two), `enable_smep_smap` | `or` and `and` write the flags. Both vendors say so |
    | 7 | `cpu.rs`: `read_cr0`, `read_cr2`, `read_cr3`, `read_cr4`, `load_cr3`, `flush_tlb_non_global`; `boot/uefi/src/main.rs`: `read_cr4` | A move to or from a control register. AMD: no flag affected. Intel: all six status flags undefined |
    | 2 | `cpu.rs`: `init_cpu_state` (the write of DR7), `read_dr7` | A move to or from a debug register: Intel says the same. The review did not name these |
    | 4 | `cpu.rs`: `fpu_save`, `fpu_restore`, two each | `xrstor` and `fxrstor` replace the x87 status word and MXCSR. `xsave` and `fxsave` go with them |
    | 2 | `cpu.rs`: `ordered_tsc`'s `lfence; rdtsc`; `iommu.rs`: `flush`'s `clflush` | Intel's entries for `lfence` and `clflush` have no "Flags Affected" section |
    | 2 | `cpu.rs`: `xmm_load`, `xmm_read` | `movq` is an SSE instruction, and AMD documents its MMX forms only in a volume that could not be used |

  - **Gate 1, the options** (`developer-tools/xtask/src/asmflags.rs`, run by the `unsafe` gate). A block that declares the option may hold only the fifteen mnemonics of `FLAG_FREE`, and `mov` only if no operand is a control or debug register. It reads the templates of `asm!`, `naked_asm!` and `global_asm!` as the assembler does: every string literal, split at line breaks and at `;`, with format placeholders taken out. It fails on what it cannot read: a template that is not a plain string literal, `att_syntax`, `raw`, a label, a directive, a prefix, an unknown escape, a block that is never closed, and the option anywhere outside those three macros.
  - **Gate 2, the files that hold `unsafe`** (`unsafety.rs`). The gate allowed the whole directory `framekernel/frame`. It now names 22 files, each with what it needs `unsafe` for, and fails on `unsafe` in any other framework file, on a framework file that is neither listed nor starts with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, on a listed file that holds none or is gone, and on a kernel crate outside the framework whose library root lacks the attribute. The attribute is read as tokens among the file's opening inner attributes; the old check was a substring search, which a comment satisfied. Seventeen framework files held no `unsafe` and did not forbid it; each gained the line. `framekernel/frame/src/lib.rs` cannot carry it (it would reach the listed modules beneath), so the gate counts that file's sites itself.
  - **Gate 3, documents** (`documents.rs`; `cargo xtask document-gate`). No tracked file is a document or an archive, by its name or by its first bytes, outside an allowlist of exact paths with reasons. The allowlist has one entry, the kernel's embedded `framekernel/assets/initramfs.tar`, and an entry nothing needs fails the gate. The branch's history is read too, by name: a document that one commit added and a later one deleted is still published by a push. In a copy of the tree that is not a git checkout, every file is read instead.
  - **Gate 4, the §11 lint** (`targetcfg.rs`, called by `linux_cfg_lint`; `cargo xtask cfg-lint`). Beside `target_os = "linux"` it refuses `unix` and `windows` as `cfg` predicates, and `target_family` and `target_env` wherever they stand, with the environment variables a build script reads them by. It reads tokens, so a condition over several lines is seen and a variable called `unix` is not. Manifests and `.cargo/config.toml` are read for the same predicates.
  - **One lexer** (`lex.rs`) under all of them, made from the one the `unsafe` gate had. That gate counts the same with it as before: 321 sites in 145 files.
- **Research:** `docs/research/2026-11-10-asm-flags.md`. Read on the day, each from its publisher: the Rust Reference as published for 1.99.1; Intel's SDM Volume 2, 325383-093US, September 2026; AMD's APM Volume 3, 24594 Rev 3.39, October 2026, and Volume 4, 26568 Rev 3.27, July 2026. Sizes and SHA-256 are in the ledger. AMD's Volume 5 (26569 Rev 3.16) is served as public and marked "AMD Confidential - Distribution with NDA" on every page: it was not used, and the copy was deleted. No operating-system source was opened (§3). The manuals were kept in the session's scratch directory and deleted at the end; none is in the repository.
- **What it did to the built code:** nothing. The base (`2fbaea6`) and the changed source were built in one directory with Rust 1.99.1, so that paths and symbol names match.
  - Kernel (`x86_64-unknown-none`, release, 1,203,984 bytes): the two files differ in 2 bytes, both the line number in a panic location of `cpu.rs` (718 to 729, 721 to 732), because comments moved the code down eleven lines. `.text` (764,036 bytes) is identical, and so is the disassembly.
  - Loader (`x86_64-unknown-uefi`, release, `test-trust-store`, 175,616 bytes): the disassembly is identical. The files differ in 10 to 12 bytes from one build to the next, all of them the link time in the PE header and the linker's debug identifier. Two builds of the same source differ in those bytes too, so the loader is not reproducible bit for bit today: a finding for §75, not part of this task.
  - Rebuilding the base source a second time gave the first kernel again, byte for byte (SHA-256 `a0faf324…7f461`).
- **Negative controls on the real tree,** each planted, run through the quick command and undone:
  - *Options:* the old option put back on `load_page_tables` and on the loader's `read_cr4`. The gate named `or` twice, the moves from and to `cr0`, the move to `cr3`, and the loader's move from `cr4`.
  - *Files:* the attribute deleted from `frames.rs`; an `unsafe` block added to the crate root `lib.rs`; a new framework file with neither a listing nor the attribute; the attribute deleted from `runtime/abi/src/lib.rs`; the attribute turned into a comment in `sync/src/wait.rs`; the attribute weakened to `deny` in `apic.rs`. Each failed with the file's name. Beside the gate, the compiler refused an `unsafe` block added to `apic.rs` and to `sync/src/refcount.rs`, two of the seventeen, naming the new attribute.
  - *Documents:* a file starting `%PDF-` staged as `docs/planted-control.pdf` (forced past `.gitignore`), the same bytes staged as `.txt`, and a ZIP staged. Each failed, the second "by its first bytes". The same PDF untracked in `specifications/` passed, as it should.
  - *The lint:* `#[cfg(unix)]` in `runtime/abi`; `target_env` in the loader's library; `target_family` over three lines in the kernel library; `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` in a manifest; a `target_os = "linux"` table in `.cargo/config.toml`; the old text in `services/directory`. Each failed with its file and line. `#[cfg(unix)]` under `developer-tools/` passed, as it should.
  - **One slip, caught and undone.** The first run of the file controls restored the tree with `git checkout -- framekernel runtime`, which also threw away the seventeen attribute lines, not yet committed. Controls B to E of that run therefore ran on a tree without them and proved nothing. The lines were put back by the same script, the change was committed, and all six controls were run again on the committed tree, each restoring only the file it touched. The results above are from that second run.
- **Unit tests:** 43 new in `xtask` (114 in all): the lexer 8; the options gate 12, among them the option put back on every block of the real framework and loader; the `unsafe` gate 7 new beside its 6; the document gate 9, one of which makes a real repository, stages a PDF, commits it, deletes it by a later commit and drops the commits; the lint 7.

The gates' own lines: the §11 lint over 216 Rust files and 17 manifests outside `developer-tools/`; the document gate over 418 tracked files and 40 paths the branch's history added and no longer has; the `unsafe` gate, 321 sites in the 22 files listed and none in the framework's other 32; the options gate, 18 of 79 assembly blocks. ## Speculation and processor hardening, the first code (ADR-0017 Z1, Z2, Z3, Z5, Z9, Z10; TASKS item 19b; 2026-11-10)

- **What:** on `claude/intelligent-dhawan-a7f6d4`, on top of 19a's documents (`3a72ae4` to `da0d6b0`). The contract is in TASKS item 19, written before the code, with what changed from it while building.
  - `framekernel/frame/src/nospec.rs` (new, safe): an index, a count or an address that a program chose, kept in range on a path the processor took by guessing a check wrong. Two forms: a conditional move that depends on the comparison (`Form::Mask`), or the check and then LFENCE (`Form::Fence`). `choose` picks by maker and family, as ADR-0017 Z9's table has it; the form is Fence until the boot processor sets it. On a host the same results come from plain Rust.
  - `framekernel/frame/src/speculation.rs` (new, safe): `Reported`, what a processor was asked; `Plan::decide`, what the kernel sets from it and what the processor lacks; each processor's plan and whether its registers read back, in one atomic word; `Ledger`, one processor's count of changes of process, with its changes and barriers in one word so another processor reads them together.
  - `framekernel/frame/src/cpu.rs`: `below_or_zero` (CMP, CMOVAE) and `after_fence` (LFENCE), the two sequences; `read_speculation`; `init_speculation`, called from `load_tables` on every processor; `entering_process` and `issue_ibpb`; thirteen `xor`s, a `test` and a `cmovnz` in `exception_saved`; an INT3 after each hand-written RET, the far RET in `load_tables` and the IRETQ.
  - `framekernel/frame/src/userspace.rs` (`copy_in`, `copy_out`), `framekernel/src/handles.rs` (`get`, `remove`) and `framekernel/src/syscall.rs` (three counts): the callers. `framekernel/src/sched.rs`: one call in `follow_thread`.
  - `framekernel/src/kernel.rs`: `prove_speculation`, `prove_nospec` and `prove_ibpb`; `framekernel/src/bootproof.rs`: their three rows.
  - `.cargo/config.toml`: `-C jump-tables=no` and `-C target-feature=+harden-sls-ret` for the kernel's target.
  - `developer-tools/xtask/src/image.rs` (new): the gate on the kernel's image, in `cargo xtask check` and as `cargo xtask image-gate [ELF]`.
- **Specifications:** `docs/research/2026-11-10-speculation-processor-hardening.md`, with each document's revision, date, size and hash. For the code: Intel SDM Volume 4 (335592-093) for MSRs 48H, 49H and 10AH, and Volume 1 (253665-093) for CPUID leaf 07H; AMD's APM Volume 2 (24593, Rev. 3.46) §3.1.7 and §3.2.9 and Volume 3 (24594, Rev. 3.39) for Fn0000_0001, Fn8000_0008 and Fn8000_0021; Intel's and AMD's guidance on bounds checks; AMD's white paper on managing speculation (revision 5.09.23), mitigations G-1, G-2 and G-5, read again for the code (ledger §3.14). The test vectors are AMD's published register values for Family 1Ah Model 51h (publication 58264, Rev 0.45) and Model 02h (57238, Rev 0.49). The Intel vectors are built from the SDM's bit positions: no Intel processor's own values were read.

- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none. No operating system's source and no other project's was opened for this, in 19a or 19b. `harden-sls-ret` is the code generator's own name for the feature, found by asking the compiler (ledger R1).
- **`unsafe`:** thirteen new sites, all in `cpu.rs`: the two sequences, one `rdmsr` in `read_speculation`, eight `rdmsr` and `wrmsr` in `init_speculation`, and one `wrmsr` each in `entering_process` and `issue_ibpb`. The gate counts 334 sites in the framework, 321 before. The two new modules forbid `unsafe`. No new block declares `preserves_flags`, and no `options(…)` line of an existing block changed.
  - *Soundness of the safe interfaces:* `below_or_zero` and `after_fence` touch registers only. `read_speculation` reads CPUID, and `IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES` only where CPUID.07H.00H:EDX[29] reports it. `init_speculation` is private, and writes each register only where `Plan::decide` found the bit that enumerates it: `IA32_SPEC_CTRL` where any bit of it is enumerated, with only enumerated bits set; EFER.AIBRSE where Fn8000_0021_EAX[8] is 1; AMD's MSR C001_1029 only on a family AMD says has it, where LFENCE is not reported as serializing and no hypervisor runs the processor. `entering_process` needs the scheduler's `Switch` token, so it runs only at the switch point with interrupts off, and writes `IA32_PRED_CMD` only where the processor recorded that it has IBPB. `issue_ibpb` writes the same register under the same condition. Nothing these write can widen what a processor speculates on.
- **Limits, stated plainly:**
  - **No control has been written on a processor that has it.** QEMU 11.1.3's software processor reports no `IA32_SPEC_CTRL`, no IBPB, no `IA32_ARCH_CAPABILITIES` and no automatic IBRS, so every boot on the development machine prints `on: nothing` and issues no barrier. The paths that write a register have run nowhere. CI's boots under KVM were expected to be the first, and were not. On 2026-11-11 the review batch's CI ran its real-CPU boots at `55db1f1` on an AMD EPYC 7763 (family 25) and an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C (family 6, model 207), each as a guest under KVM with `-cpu max`. The guests offered none of the controls: every boot printed `on: nothing; ... not offered: enhanced or automatic IBRS, IBPB, branch isolation between sibling threads` and `this processor has no IBPB to measure`. So the paths that write a register have still run nowhere, and GitHub's runners cannot run them. A guest there would in any case be a guest on a server processor, not hardware in the declared scope (§74).
  - **No test shows what a processor does on a wrongly guessed path.** The proofs show what the two sequences compute. That they hold under speculation rests on Intel's and AMD's documents.
  - **The toolchain's prebuilt `core`, `alloc` and `compiler_builtins` are outside the image rules** (ADR-0017 Amendment 1, item 152): 113 returns, 33 without an INT3, and 2 jump tables in this image.
  - The IBPB proof checks the kernel's own count, not the register. Under QEMU the count of barriers is zero by rule, so "one barrier for each change" is shown by the host test of `Ledger` only.
  - The pass after a resume from sleep (Z1) is not built: there is no sleep yet. Nor is the typed interface that will serve these facts.
  - The costs the boot prints are an emulator's.

## The many-page unmap proof no longer depends on timing (the review batch's first CI run; 2026-11-10)

- **What:** `framekernel/src/aspace.rs`, the boot proof `unmap_many` and one new program for it, `read_again_when_told`. No kernel code outside the proof changes, and the line the proof prints and the boot test expects is the same.
  - **Before:** the proof's thread read its page, the last of the range, in a loop while the range was unmapped, and the proof expected one interrupt for each round of 128 pages.
  - **What went wrong:** with more than one round, an earlier round flushes every translation of the space on the thread's processor, its own page's among them. If that processor was then slow to go back to its thread, the last round had cleared the entries by the time the thread read again: it faulted by itself and left the space, no processor held the space when the round asked, and the round interrupted none. The kernel did nothing wrong, and the proof failed the boot.
  - **Now:** the thread reads its page once, so that its processor holds a translation for it, keeps off the page until `unmap` has returned, and reads it again when told. Every round finds it running, so the count is exact, and the fault it takes at the second read shows that the translation it held is gone.
- **Where it was seen:** the first CI run of pull request 15, at `9de1def`, job "boots on a real CPU (ubuntu-24.04)", the boot with the AMD IOMMU and the NIC behind a bridge: `200 pages unmapped at once under a running thread on another processor: it faulted at its page among them: true; Ok(Change { pages: 200, shootdowns: 2, interrupts: 1 }): address spaces failed`. Seven other boots of the same job printed `interrupts: 2`. The proof is task S3-5a's and was the same on every branch.
- **Specifications:** none new. The rounds, and the flush for more than 32 pages, are `UserSpace::unmap`'s and `origin_sync::shootdown`'s own (the section "Address spaces that change while they run" above).
- **Architecture decisions:** ADR-0013 R1 (a proof must not fail on a correct kernel) and its controls C34 to C36. ADR-0004 H2 and ADR-0011 N14 step 3 are unchanged.
- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none.
- **`unsafe`:** none. The new program is 48 bytes of ring-3 machine code in a `Vec`: `read_later_when_told` with one read added before its loop, in the instruction encodings the file's other programs use.
- **A first attempt, not kept:** accepting one interrupt fewer on the last of several rounds. A control showed what it cost: with every round after the first asking nobody while the thread still ran, the count was one the relaxed check accepted, and the boot failed only because the thread did not fault within the wait. The exact count catches that outright, so the proof was changed to keep it exact.
- **Limits, stated plainly:**
  - The interleaving was reproduced only by planting two waits (C34). Without them no boot on the development machine has shown it.
  - On real processors the changed proof has run only as a guest under KVM: in CI at `55db1f1`, on an AMD EPYC 7763 and an Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, 34 boots printed the 200-page line with `interrupts: 2` on another processor and 4 with `interrupts: 0` on one processor, and none failed.
  - The single-round proofs in the same file still have a thread reading its page throughout. No earlier round flushes its translation there, and none has been seen to fail. A processor that lost the translation another way in the few instructions between the change and the request would fail them the same way.
  - A thread that still held a stale translation could lose it another way before it is told to read (a processor that reloads CR3 drops it), and would then fault although the shootdown did nothing. C36 was caught on its one boot; that catch depends on the translation surviving until the read.
  - No human has reviewed this.
- **Test evidence (2026-11-10; Rust 1.99.1, QEMU 11.1.3 TCG + OVMF, 2 processors, Intel VT-d):** each control is a temporary edit to an exported copy of the tree that has the change, built and booted once, with the proof's own failing line taken out of the copy's `boot_failures` so that the boot ran on to the refusal. The lines are from the serial logs.
  - *C34, the interleaving forced against the proof as it was:* `... interrupts: 1 }): address spaces failed`, CI's line. With the same two waits and the changed proof: `... interrupts: 2 })`, and `cargo xtask boot-test` passes, 11 of 11.
  - *C35, every round after the first asks nobody:* `... it faulted at its page among them: true; Ok(Change { pages: 200, shootdowns: 2, interrupts: 1 }): address spaces failed`.
  - *C36, a processor answers without dropping anything:* `... it faulted at its page among them: false; Ok(Change { pages: 200, shootdowns: 2, interrupts: 2 }): address spaces failed`.
  - *C19 and C21 again, on the changed proof:* `interrupts: 0` with no fault on the 5-page and 200-page lines; `interrupts: 3` and `6` with 4 processors. Each ends `boot refused: live address spaces failed`.
  - *The unedited copy:* `5 pages ... interrupts: 1 })`, `200 pages ... interrupts: 2 })`, and `cargo xtask boot-test` passes, 11 of 11.
  - *The landing tree at `3138dd9`, with a clean tree before and after:* `cargo xtask check` passes (1,312 host tests, 0 failed, 10 ignored; the gates; Loom), and `cargo xtask boot-test` passes, 11 of 11, with 2 processors and again with 1, where the thread shares the unmapping processor: `200 pages ... on this processor: ... Ok(Change { pages: 200, shootdowns: 2, interrupts: 0 })`. `boot-matrix` was not run on the development machine.

## The channel quota's count, tested on the host, and a charge that takes its sum only under the quota (2026-11-11)

- **What:** `framekernel/src/quota.rs` (new) and `framekernel/src/process.rs`, whose `Account` now counts its channels with it. Two commits: `a856e0d`, the move, and `4dbbb59`, the fix.
  - **The move:** `process.rs` is built only for the kernel's target, so nothing in it can have a host test. A process's count of channels against its quota is now `quota::Count` (`charge`, `refund`, `held`), in a module the host builds too, as `mapping.rs` holds the memory quotas' arithmetic for `process.rs`. `Account::charge_channel` and `refund_channel` stay and call it, so `ipc.rs` is unchanged. `lib.rs` gains the module's line and its line in the module list.
  - **The fault:** the charge was `(n < max).then_some(n + 1)`, and `then_some` evaluates its argument before the comparison is looked at. A refund of something never charged wraps the count to the top of its range, and the next charge then overflows the sum. A build that checks overflow panics there. One that does not wraps the sum, drops it and answers `limit`. The boot images are built with the release profile and the workspace sets no `overflow-checks`, so the kernel as booted already refused; a kernel built with the dev profile would have panicked, as the host test did.
  - **Now:** the sum is taken only once the count is under its quota (`if n < self.max { Some(n + 1) } else { None }`), so the answer is `limit` in every build. A refund too many fails closed, and `refund`'s documentation says so.
- **How it was found:** the count quotas of task S3-6, which are not in this batch, were first written in the same form, and their refund test panicked. No refund too many is known in the kernel.
- **Specifications:** none. `bool::then_some` and `AtomicUsize::try_update` are as the standard library documents them for Rust 1.99.1.
- **Architecture decisions:** ADR-0005 P11 (a process's creator sets its quotas). No decision changes.
- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none.
- **`unsafe`:** none. `quota.rs` starts with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
- **Limits, stated plainly:**
  - Nothing a program can observe changes: the kernel as booted gives the same answers before and after.
  - The new test fails without the fix only in a build that checks overflow. That is the profile the gates test with. With `--release` the old form passes it, by the wrapped sum.
  - The other two charges in `process.rs`, `charge_queued` and `charge_committed`, use `checked_add` and were not at fault. They stay in `process.rs`, with no host test of their own.
  - The thread test runs on the host's threads and is not a Loom model. The step it tests is one `try_update`.
  - A refund too many is not detected or reported. It only fails closed.
  - No human has reviewed this.
- **Test evidence (2026-11-11; Rust 1.99.1; the boots under QEMU TCG + OVMF on the M1 Max):** every run held the machine's turn, with a clean tree before and after.
  - *Each of the two commits, 12:39 to 12:40 UTC:* `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy` with `-D warnings` is clean for the kernel on the host (`--lib --tests`), for the kernel on `x86_64-unknown-none` and for xtask (`--all-targets`). `cargo test --package framekernel --lib`: 425 passed at `a856e0d` and 426 at `4dbbb59`, none failed. `cargo test --package xtask`: 145 passed, 1 ignored.
  - *Control for the fix, the tip's tests on the charge as it was:* `a_refund_too_many_refuses_every_later_charge ... FAILED`, `attempt to add with overflow` at the sum; the other five passed. The file was put back and compared byte for byte.
  - *Control for the thread test, the charge as a load, a yield and a store:* `charges_from_several_threads_never_pass_the_quota ... FAILED`: the count after every charge was refunded was not 0. Put back the same way.
  - *`cargo xtask check` at `4dbbb59`, 12:40 to 12:47 UTC:* passed. Its host tests' result lines sum to 1,376 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored; the gates passed; Loom ran its 42 models and caught its 68 negative controls. None of the Loom models is of this count.
  - *`cargo xtask boot-test` at `4dbbb59`, 12:47 to 12:49 UTC:* passed, 11 of 11 scenarios. The kernel's own proof of the channel quota printed `ipc: quotas: a fifth channel -> LIMIT, a thirteenth handle -> LIMIT, one more after a close -> OK, still working -> OK`, as before. The verdict is the usual one under QEMU: degraded, 60 of 61 proofs, speculation controls failed (item 154).
  - *Not run:* a boot at `a856e0d`, the boot matrix, anything on a real processor.
  - *In the batch:* merged into `land/s3-part2` on 2026-11-11 at `d8e9d49`, after the coordinating session read it, and before the S3-6 task branch that also holds it (merged there at `ac473c7`), so nothing came twice. The kernel's host tests passed right after that merge (422 passed, 0 failed). The gates on the merge that followed, `15baed9`, are in the next entry. No person has reviewed it.

## The requirements matrix and its gate (TASKS item 35; CLAUDE.md §1; decision items 191 to 196; 2026-11-12)

- **What:** on `claude/dazzling-jackson-9eca1b`, from `main` at `405495c` with the decision record `docs/decisions-191-220` (`88fa0c3`) merged in. CLAUDE.md §1 measures coverage against a versioned requirements matrix, and there was none. There is now:
  - **The matrix,** `docs/requirements/`: a `README.md` with the rules, 22 tables for the directive (its header, its twenty PARTs and its final rules) and 17 for the accepted ADRs. 1,615 rows: one for each of CLAUDE.md 7.6's 1,382 statements and each of the ADRs' 233 decisions. Each row has an owning role, a scope, a state, its implementation, acceptance criteria, evidence, where the evidence ran, who reviewed it, its limitations and the decision items that decided it.
  - **The gate,** `developer-tools/xtask/src/requirements.rs`: `cargo xtask requirements-gate`, and a step of `cargo xtask check` beside the document gate. It finds the directive's statements and the ADRs' decisions by rule, so it holds the matrix to its sources both ways: a statement with no row fails, and so does a row whose statement is gone. It holds each state to what its row names: evidence and implementations that are in the tree, no `done` on evidence from a weaker environment than the row's scope, nothing past `not-started` without acceptance criteria. It holds every answered decision item to a row or to the README's list, every removed row to a scope change with its item, and the README's revision to the directive's. A run that reads no row fails. It prints the coverage figure.
- **The figure at this commit:** 35 of 1,563 counted rows done (2.2%), 261 built, 187 partial, 62 not verified, 1,018 not started; 51 rows ask for nothing and one is removed. Evidence ran on the host for 177 rows and in KVM guests in CI for 306, and on a physical machine for none. An AI reviewer's record covers 263 of the 545 rows past not-started, and a person has reviewed none.
- **How the rows were written.** A script laid the first version out from the gate's own reading of the sources, so each quote is what the gate expects, with each judgement written as a rule: owner, scope, kind, state, criteria, evidence, limitations. States follow `docs/STATUS.md`, the boot proofs, the tests and the gates; a row is `done` only where a gate, a file or a CI job shows it. The tables are the only copy now (decision item 192) and are changed by hand. The script is not in the repository.
- **What the gate does not check:** whether an owner, scope, kind, criterion or state is the right judgement; whether evidence passes (that is `cargo xtask check` and the boots); where evidence ran, beyond asking a record under `docs/hardware/` of a row that says hardware; who reviewed a row; and the body of an ADR's decision changing under an unchanged title.
- **Negative controls on the real tree,** each planted in one file, run through the gate and undone by restoring that file, with everything else committed first. 19 of 19 were refused with their own message: evidence that is not in the tree; an implementation that is not in the tree; a row with no owner; an owner that is not one of the 67 roles; a row with a cell missing; an unknown state; an ID used twice; a statement with no row (a row deleted); a row whose statement is gone (CLAUDE.md §33 edited); `done` below its scope; hardware claimed with no record; `done` without acceptance criteria; a removed row without its item; a decision with no row; an ADR that gains a decision (ADR-0012 edited); an answered item no row names, two ways; another revision of the directive in the README; a scope change that names no such row. Afterwards the tree was as committed and the gate passed.
- **Unit tests:** 32 new in `xtask`. A small sound matrix with every state, kind and kind of evidence passes and is counted exactly; then one fault at a time: rows that do not parse (19 forms), a file that is not a table of the matrix, no row read, an owner that is no role, an ID used twice, evidence and implementations not in the tree, each state's needs, `done` at and below its scope, statements and rows that do not match (also the same words twice, and a removed row that outlives its statement), rows out of their file or their source's order, decisions with no row or another title, an ADR that is not accepted, items unnamed, unanswered or listed twice, scope changes, the revision, a README without its tables, unreadable sources, and long lists of problems cut short. - **What:** E1 as the owner accepted it on 2026-11-10, built as task S4-0 of ADR-0011 N14 step 4 (`docs/research/2026-11-11-n14-step4-scope.md`, section 4, whose exit tests were written before the code).   - `fdca8af` the §78 contract.
  - `86a2f66` the change itself, in one commit because the type crosses every crate: `origin-abi` (`Handle` is `u64`; `received_handle` is `{u64 handle; u32 object_type; u32 rights}`, 16 bytes; a start entry is `{u64 handle; u32 object_type; u32 rights; u32 role}` and four bytes of zero padding, 24 bytes, which the decoder refuses when not zero); `origin.kernel.oidl` (the two handle fields are `u64`) and its lock; `origin-version.toml`; the generator (`rt::Handle` is a `u64` in memory, `origin_handle_t` a `uint64_t`, a handle register is no longer refused for its upper 32 bits, in the generated decoder and in the corpus's independent model, and the corpus checker reads 64-bit handle values); `framekernel/syscalls` and `sdk/directory` regenerated; the kernel's table (`handles.rs`: the slot index plus one in the top 24 bits, the generation in the low 40; a slot retired after 2^40 − 1 generations instead of 2^16 − 1; the free list holds `u32` indexes); `syscall.rs` (handles copied in and out as `u64`s, each record's handle at its own offset); the proofs (the script interpreter loads all 64 bits of a handle, a pseudo-step copies one, and the handle slots move from `u32`s at `DATA` to `u64`s in an area of their own at `DATA + 0x3000`, because the ping-pong programs keep their own layout at `DATA`); the directory service's tests (handle values above 32 bits); and the generator's test programs.
  - `6fe4a74` the boot exit test: the hostile process is given a live channel end; a wait on it is `ok`, and on its low 32 bits alone, and on its slot at a generation never issued, `bad_handle`. The check that another process's handle is slot 40 reads the slot from the top of the value.
  - `380e27c` `docs/spec/OIDL.md` §10, revised as E1 says.
  - the records: this entry, TASKS, STATUS, the system-call threat model (H1, H2 and the Z9 list), ADR-0013's evidence (H64-1, H64-2), `OIDL_KERNEL_COMPARISON.md`'s status, and the matrix rows A05-E1, A05-B3 and A05-C4.
- **Specifications:** none outside the repository. ADR-0005 P1, P4, B3, C4 and Amendment 6 (E1); ADR-0011 N9 and Amendment 2 (L5); `docs/spec/OIDL.md` §3.1, §5, §9, §10, §13, §14.

- **`unsafe`:** none added. The only assembly changed is the proof interpreter's, in `framekernel/frame/src/proof_programs.rs`, already on the gate's list.
- **Decisions this task did not take:** none of the owner's. Where E1 left a choice to the kernel it took E1's own example, 24 bits of slot and 40 of generation, and put the slot on top, so that a value cut to 32 bits names no slot and any 32-bit path left in the kernel, the generated code or the proofs fails loudly (controls H64-1, below). ## TASKS item 39: the fingerprint records a handle's width, `oidl-fingerprint 2` (decision item 237; 2026-11-12)

- **What:** on `claude/item-39-fingerprint-width`, from `records/item-237` at `e306ab7`, which sits on the third batch's merge of S4-0 (`5871257`). OIDL §13's canonical description did not record how wide a handle is, so `origin.kernel` 0.7's digest came out equal to 0.6's after S4-0. The owner accepted recording it (item 237). Commits:
  - `85fa8a9` the generator: `layout::HANDLE_BITS` (64), from which the description's new line `handle <bits>` comes, after `transport`, and from which the generator emits a handle's Rust ABI type and C's `origin_handle_t`. A test holds the runtime template's `Handle` to the same width. `FORMAT` is `oidl-fingerprint 2`, and the pinned digest moves with it. Both locks recorded again.
  - `3978849` the specification and the records: OIDL §13's text in place of its dated note, and a revisions entry; TASKS item 39; the matrix row A11-N13; this entry. Then `records/item-237` at `8977f4f` merged in, with TASKS item 39's corrected criteria.
- **Specifications:** none outside the repository. `docs/spec/OIDL.md` §9, §10, §13; ADR-0005 E1; ADR-0011 N13; decision item 237.
- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none.
- **`unsafe`:** none.
- **Decisions this task did not take:** whether `origin.kernel` 0.7's digest should differ from 0.6's. The first wording of TASKS item 39 asked for it, and item 237 as decided cannot give it: the width is the specification's, not a library's, so every minor's description carries today's 64 bits, and 0.6 and 0.7 still share `d270a7a5…`. Making them differ would need a definition to say when its width changed, which is a question of grammar. This session put that to the coordinating session on 2026-11-12, recommending that the criterion be dropped. That session agreed: it corrected TASKS item 39's criteria on `records/item-237` at `8977f4f`, merged here, and put no grammar change to the owner.
- **Limits:** the width is one number for both transports. A `channel` slot is a position, 4 bytes, and its width is in the layout already; the `handle` line describes the values a transport delivers. Nothing describes a width per minor.
- **Test evidence (2026-11-12; Rust 1.99.1; the M1 Max):**
  - `oidl`'s unit tests, 51 passed: `the_description_records_the_handle_width_the_generator_emits` (every minor of both shipped libraries, stable and release, says `handle 64` after `transport`; the runtime template's `Handle` is a `u64` of 8 bytes; the kernel's C header says `uint64_t`), and the negative control `a_planted_handle_width_changes_every_digest` (a 32-bit width changes every minor's stable and release digest of both libraries). Its `generated` suite, 19 passed.
  - A planted change, once: `HANDLE_BITS` set to 32 in `layout.rs`, then `cargo xtask interface-gate`, which failed: "the ABI of origin.kernel is not the one sdk/interfaces/origin.kernel.lock records". Put back byte for byte.
  - The locks recorded again: every digest of `origin.kernel` (0.0 to 0.7) and of `origin.directory` (0.0, 0.1) differs from its format-1 value; `origin.kernel` 0.6 and 0.7 are equal, as above.

## `cargo xtask`: the expected `harden-sls-ret` warning collapsed to one line (2026-11-12)

- **What:** `run_step` reads a command's error output line by line. `developer-tools/xtask/src/expected_warning.rs` drops exactly the compiler's five-line warning that `-C target-feature=+harden-sls-ret` (ADR-0017 Z10) is unknown and unstable, and each crate's "generated 1 warning" summary while that is the build's only warning, and prints one note in their place. Every other line passes through in order; once any other warning appears, no summary is dropped for the rest of that command.
- **Why:** the owner's choice on 2026-11-12, "Collapse to one line", over leaving twelve copies in every build's output. Stable Rust 1.99.1 has no supported option for the feature and no lint governs the warning (`-A` cannot silence it); removing the option would remove the protection. The image gate (`image.rs`) still holds the protection.
- **Tests:** six host tests: CI's own output (run 43118681550), another warning passing through, a near-miss passing through in order, other counts, colour codes, and the note's words. In real output on the development Mac, the boot test's kernel build printed one note, "(warnings: 1, crate summaries: 12)", and no copy of the warning.

## TASKS item 22a: the toolchain checks in CI, and §10's `wcslen` test inside the loader (CLAUDE.md §8 to §10; decision items 123 and 252; 2026-11-12)

- **What:**

Its header lists the four places a compiler upgrade changes together (§15), the commit file among them: nothing else in the tree says what an upgrade changes. The inspection of the stand-alone object is gone, and `tests/toolchain/uefi_smoke.rs` is §9's link test only (the table under "`tests/toolchain/`" above still gives it both roles).

- **Specifications:** CLAUDE.md §8, §9 and §10. The regressions are as `docs/research/2026-11-07-onbf.md` records them (R2, T5), not read again. No external specification, and no reference code, was read for this task.
- **Architecture decisions:** none of its own (no ABI or format is touched, §84). Decision item 123 for what CI must run; item 252 for the roadmap's tests M0-1 to M0-3; ADR-0002 for why the loop stays off the boot path: the one `CHAR16` string the loader measures is the firmware's vendor name, and that keeps its bounded copy.
- **Dependencies:** none new. `llvm-nm` and `llvm-objdump` come with the pinned `llvm-tools`. The workflow gains no action, no secret and no permission.
- **Toolchain:** rustc 1.99.1 (`58cf8f9c35b355199727627d07ae34a4e2846d67`, LLVM 23.1.1), cargo 1.99.1 (`5f94df478`), rustup 1.29.3, on macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Max.

- **Performance cost (ADR-0018 V3):**
  - **Every image: none, by construction, and checked.** Two copies of the tree without git, at the same path, one of `0550226` and one of `b52c36c`, each built with `cargo build --locked --release` for its target. All four files are the same bytes:

    | Image | SHA-256 at `0550226` and at `b52c36c` | Bytes |
    |---|---|---|
    | `origin-boot.efi`, no feature | `d6b62ba20e4da61b779e3fdd9ef2d11d27471bb623e922b3b361a4d467e7feea` | 196,096 |
    | `origin-boot.efi`, `test-trust-store` | `7b9a7207135e5cf211bfe76165d916a8c861900cc40d1272b3f4f02d4874998a` | 199,168 |
    | `origin-boot.efi`, `developer-mode` | `9e4ebbc896df22891bcbc76ac29f4dbf302970bc2bc408a2374392aca6df60af` | 199,168 |
    | `framekernel` (ELF) | `f7b07acf528e904122496e6a3c89b880e843433bd166e334a2d9c81564572375` | 1,642,080 |

    So no boot was needed, and none was run.
  - **The build host: measured.** The whole of `verify.sh`, the loader's build from nothing included, takes about 3.1 s on the M1 Max (two runs timed on 2026-11-12, 3.13 s and 3.15 s, before the comparison of the three places was added). No budget is set.
  - **CI: unmeasured, owed.** One more job. Its time is read from the first run.
- **How the `wcslen` test works, and what was tried to choose it** (in copies of the tree without git; none of the trial code is in the tree):
  - For `x86_64-unknown-uefi`, LLVM 23.1.1 compiles `char16_len` to a jump to `wcslen`: the library's object holds `T …char16_len` and `U wcslen`, and the function's disassembly is three instructions and a `jmp` with the relocation `IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 wcslen`.
  - The loader's link needs that symbol although nothing calls the function. With the function's body replaced by a call to `wcslen_absent`, which nothing defines: `rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: wcslen_absent >>> referenced by liborigin_boot_uefi-….rlib(….rcgu.o):(origin_boot_uefi::uefi::char16_len)`. The linker resolves every symbol of an object it loads, and only then drops what nothing calls. On a toolchain with no `wcslen`, which is the regression, the loader would fail to link the same way.
  - The function is not in the image: the digests above.
  - **The loop's form matters.** With `n += 1` and `-C overflow-checks=yes`, the library's object holds no `U wcslen`: the check gives the loop a second way out, and LLVM leaves it a loop. With `n = n.wrapping_add(1)`, the form committed, the call is there with the checks off and on, and the image equals the one without the function both times (`d6b62ba2…` off, `e7c29d4d…` on). The second half of TASKS item 22 turns those checks on for the loader, so the test would have stopped testing then.
  - **`verify.sh` checks on every run that the test still tests,** before it trusts the link: the code of `char16_len`, in the library's object, names `wcslen`; and the library is one object, so the object that holds the loop is the one the loader takes everything else from. If either fails, the result is a FAIL and the link is recorded as showing nothing.
- **What `--locked` covers.** Every cargo command the two workflows give carries it, in front of the alias (`cargo --locked xtask …`), and `verify.sh`'s own loader builds pass it. The first such command of a job resolves the whole workspace against the root `Cargo.lock`, which holds the workspace's packages alone (`cargo xtask check`'s dependency check). The cargo commands `xtask` starts afterwards resolve the same workspace against the same file, so they have nothing to change, and they do not repeat the flag. The Loom models are the one other resolution: a scratch workspace built from the one other Cargo lock file the tree tracks, `developer-tools/xtask/src/loom.lock`, which `loom.rs` already holds with `--locked`, and with `--offline` once its crates are fetched. **What the "checkout as committed" step adds:** `--locked` says the lock file fitted the manifests when a command started. It cannot say that nothing the job ran afterwards rewrote the file, or any other tracked file. The step does, for the two jobs that do not boot; the `check` job runs every build the boot jobs do.
- **Test evidence** (development Mac; nothing here ran in CI, on Linux or on a physical x86-64 machine):
  - **Host tests:** `cargo test --package origin-boot-uefi --lib`: 47 passed (two new: lengths 0, 1, 2 and 6 from one buffer, and agreement with the bounded copy for every length from 0 to 40).
  - **`verify.sh` on a tree with nothing uncommitted,** at `b17dc8d`: PASS 20, FAIL 0, INFO 5. That run is `docs/toolchain/VERIFICATION.md`. (It was recorded three times, each from a clean tree, so that the record comes from the script the tree holds: at `8a8ca93` and at `60c6808` with PASS 19, and at `b17dc8d` once the script compared the three places the version is written.)
  - **`cargo --locked xtask check`,** in a turn on the machine, at `b52c36c`: passed in 546 s. 1,587 host tests passed and none failed; the reproducible-build gate gave the four digests above again, this time in the git tree; all 53 Loom models passed and all 78 negative controls were caught; and `git status` was empty afterwards, which is what `checkout-unchanged.sh` asks of the job.
  - **CI's install script on the Mac,** with stand-ins for `lscpu`, `nproc` and the install itself (so that a shared machine's toolchain was not touched): exit 0, and its summary line names `rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13)`. `ci.yml` and `processor-sweep.yml` parse as YAML; `permissions` is still `contents: read`.
  - **Negative controls,** each planted in a copy of `525f314` (g: of `b52c36c`) that has no git and was deleted afterwards. `verify.sh` exits 1 in every one:

    | | Planted | Result |
    |---|---|---|
    | a | The commit file holds forty zeros | `verify.sh`: `FAIL  rustc reports the pinned commit (pinned 0000…, reported 58cf8f9c…)`, PASS 18, FAIL 1. `install-rust.sh`: `::error::rustc reports commit 58cf8f9c…; the pinned commit is 0000…`, exit 1, before its target check |
    | a | The commit file holds `58cf8f9c3`; then no file | `verify.sh`: `FAIL  The pinned commit is 40 hexadecimal digits in developer-tools/toolchain/rustc-commit-hash`, both times. `install-rust.sh`: `… does not hold one commit of 40 hexadecimal digits`, then `… is missing`; exit 1 both times |
    | b | One dependency line (`"origin-abi"`, under `oidl`) out of `Cargo.lock` | `cargo --locked xtask cfg-lint`: `error: cannot update the lock file … because --locked was passed to prevent this`, exit 101, the file still as planted. `verify.sh`: both `wcslen` results FAIL (its builds pass `--locked`). `cargo xtask cfg-lint`, without the flag: exit 0, and cargo had rewritten the file to the committed text |
    | c | The loop given a bound (`\|\| n == 4096`) | `FAIL  §10 wcslen: the loader no longer exercises #163614`: the function's code is a loop and names no `wcslen`. The link is then recorded as INFO, "shows nothing about #163614 in this run" |
    | d | The loop replaced by a call to `wcslen_absent` | Both `wcslen` results FAIL; the link's evidence is the linker's `undefined symbol: wcslen_absent`, referenced by `char16_len` |
    | d | The loop kept, and a second uncalled function that calls `wcslen_absent` | The first `wcslen` result passes and the link FAILs, with `undefined symbol: wcslen_absent`, referenced by `planted`. This is the control for "the object reaches the link" by itself |
    | e | `ffi_bool.rs` as the body Rust 1.99.0 produced, in assembly (`mov eax, edi; ret`) | `FAIL  §10 FFI bool return is reduced to 0 or 1` on all three targets |
    | f | `verify.sh`'s path of `rust-lld` pointed at a name that does not exist | `FAIL  rust-lld is present in the toolchain`, PASS 18, FAIL 1 |
    | g | `rust-version` in `Cargo.toml` left at `1.98.0` (in a copy of `b52c36c` with the comparison added) | `FAIL  The pin is written the same in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml and this script`, PASS 19, FAIL 1 |

  - **Two plants did not work the first time, and are recorded as they went.** For (e), the first plant returned the byte through `transmute::<u8, bool>`: the check failed on `x86_64-unknown-uefi` only, because for the two System V targets rustc 1.99.1 still emits `andb $0x1, %al`. That is the fix for issue 163911 doing its work, and the assembly plant is the one that shows the check on every target. For (f), the first attempt's `grep` matched nothing, so nothing was planted and the script passed; it was planted again with an asserted replacement.
- **Known limits:**
  - **No CI run exists.** This task cannot push. The run on the batch's pull request is the proof of roadmap test M0-3 and of every matrix row whose criterion says CI runs something.
  - **`verify.sh` has not run on Linux with this compiler.** Its last Linux run was on 2026-11-07 under rustc 1.97.0. The first CI run is its first.

  - **`cargo xtask progress`** writes `docs/PROGRESS.md`. The page is built from the requirements matrix, CLAUDE.md's section headings, the ADRs' titles, and the roadmap's placements and state words. In order, it holds: what done, built, in progress and not started mean (decision items 193 and 221); the counted rows overall, with where their evidence ran; each milestone M0 to M13, with the state word its roadmap section gives; the fourteen feature groups of `build` rows, then each section under its group; one line per accepted ADR; and one line for the standing rules. Every figure is a count of rows, and every row counts as one. It gives two percentages, each labelled: done, and done or built. Nothing on it depends on the clock, the host or a commit (§75).
  - **`cargo xtask progress-gate`,** one line in `check`, regenerates the page in memory. It fails when the committed file differs by a byte, naming the first line that differs and the command to run.
  - **One reader of each source.** The requirements gate's loop over the matrix's files became `requirements::matrix_rows`, and the roadmap gate now reads its rows there. The parser TASKS item 42 had added is gone. The directive parser keeps each section's title, and the ADR reader keeps each ADR's title. The roadmap gate returns its placements and the milestones' headings, and `roadmap::states` reads each milestone's state word from the two forms the roadmap uses. Neither gate accepts anything it refused before. The roadmap gate also refuses a matrix the reader cannot read.
  - **The matrix README** says, under "Changing the matrix", to run the command when a row's state changes or the roadmap places a row or gives a milestone's state.
  - **Row S1-52,** in a commit of its own, at the coordinating session's request: its limitation no longer says there are no exit tests; it says what exists and what is missing. Its state stays `partial`.
- **Author / date:** Claude Code (local, M1 Max), 2026-11-12, on `claude/t43-progress-page`, cut from `5e80911`.
- **Specifications:** none outside the repository.
- **Architecture decisions:** CLAUDE.md §1 ("Maintain complete traceability", "Report verified completion"), §75, §82; decision items 122, 193, 221, 255, 256, 264; ADR-0018 V3. The fourteen groups are the coordinating session's brief. No ABI or format decision, so no ADR (§84).
- **Dependencies:** `std` only, inside `xtask`. No new crate.
- **Toolchain:** Rust 1.99.1, as the workspace pins it.
- **Review:** none. No person and no second agent has read the page or the gate.
- **Licensing:** MIT OR Apache-2.0, as the workspace.
- **Performance:** none, by construction (ADR-0018 V3): a host tool and a gate on the build host.
- **Test evidence:**
  - 9 unit tests in `progress.rs`. Among them: the counts of a small fixture; agreement with the requirements gate's own figure on this tree (counted rows, each state and each environment); and this tree's page. All 220 `xtask` tests pass, including the roadmap gate's 9 and the requirements gate's tests. The roadmap gate's fixture is now written in the matrix's thirteen columns and file names, and its assertions are unchanged.
  - The page at `666f83c` counts 1,598 rows: 47 done, 316 built, 235 in progress and 1,000 not started. The fourteen groups hold 826 `build` rows: 14 done, 122 built, 83 in progress and 607 not started. Those are the coordinating session's figures for `main` at `418aeee`. An independent Python count of the matrix and the roadmap gave the same figure in every table: overall, by environment, by group, by ADR, the standing rules, M0 to M13, and the 68 rows in no milestone.
  - Two controls planted in the real tree. Each was one edit, followed by one run of `cargo xtask progress-gate`, the function `check` calls, and each was refused (exit 1). The file was then restored with `git checkout`, and its SHA-256 matched the one taken before:

    | Control | The edit | The gate's refusal |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1 | `docs/PROGRESS.md`: Done's count changed from 47 to 48 by hand | "docs/PROGRESS.md is not the page this tree generates (they differ from line 11): run `cargo xtask progress` and commit it" |
    | 2 | `directive-03-rust-toolchain.md`: S13-02 changed from `built` to `partial`, with the page not regenerated. The requirements gate accepted the change (exit 0). | "… (they differ from line 12): run `cargo xtask progress` and commit it" |

- **External firmware/data:** none.
- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none.

Each `naked_asm!` block here has only `mov`, `pushfq`, `pop`, `jmp`, `syscall` and `ret`; none declares `preserves_flags`.
- **What `origin.core`'s dynamic table is used for at run time:** nothing. The image is a shared object only so that the linker names a program's imports. The kernel takes the bytes of its one read-execute segment and the place of each export, at build time, and nothing else of the file reaches the kernel or a process.
- **Decisions this task did not take:** none of the owner's. With the coordinating session: the class of the two new rows (Refuse, accepted), the three readings of the contract (accepted, with conditions on the first), L13's sentence on enumerations (a proposal), a trap after a stub's `ret` (a question), and the roadmap placement of A05-H1 and A11-L13 (decision item 276; this branch marks them proposed).
- **Found, for other sessions:** `image_inputs::remove_linked` does not know a `cdylib`'s second copy, `deps/liborigin_core.so`; as far as this session can see a stale one can only fail a build. The reproducible-build gate and the image-input gate took `origin.core` and the second program with no edit: 20 files and 9 carried segments, the same from two builds. Cargo places a package's own `cargo rustc -- <args>` before the shared flags, and hashes them into the unit's identity, so programs are linked against `origin.core` by a path that is the same in every checkout.
- **Limits, stated plainly:**
  - `origin.core` is not an ONBF image, and no loader maps it or reads an import table: the kernel carries it and binds from descriptions the build wrote, until the Loader Service (M6).
  - Row E8 stays open, by design, for the kernel's own proof processes (L8).
  - Only the linker's own import slots are read. A program that keeps an entry point's address in data does not build.
  - The gate on carried programs is hygiene. A linear sweep can be put out of step by data among code; a pair of `syscall`'s bytes in a gap of under 15 bytes between two sections' code would pass as inside the instruction before it. The pin stops both.
  - The gates read the toolchain's disassembly as text.
  - L13 at boot: 32-bit bits types in the second, third and fourth registers only. An enumeration is extended as its underlying integer.
  - The hostile steps of the events-and-ports proof are not run again through the stubs, and one step of the hostile IPC script is left out.
  - The hostile memory script maps at a fixed address inside the programs' region; a launch that fell on its two pages would fail the proof, about once in 10^8 boots.
  - The cost figures resolve nothing (ADR-0013).
  - What a processor does on a wrongly guessed pin comparison is row I2's, which stays Partly.
  - Nothing has run under KVM or on a real processor, and CI has not built this. No review has happened yet.
- **Test evidence (2026-11-13; Rust 1.99.1; QEMU 11.1.3 TCG + OVMF on the M1 Max):**
  - *Host:* the generator, 23 tests, among them each stub of `origin.kernel` compared with its disassembly, each narrow type in each of the six registers against a table written by hand, and the pin run over every number and offset. `onbf-pack`, 113 unit tests and 3 that compile and link with the pinned toolchain and the userspace flags: a library of naked stubs, one that is more than its stubs, and a program against it. `xtask`'s `corestubs`, 19, on listings and bytes made by hand. `framekernel` (host), 447, among them 5 of `core_image` and 13 of `program`. In each, the fixture is the planted mistake: a second `syscall` in a stub, the pair outside every stub or inside another instruction, a stub that loads another number, an instruction that is neither its extension nor the move, an extension missing or wrong, an offset the table does not hold, a function that is no stub, a relocation, writable data with bytes in the file and writable memory with none, an import outside RELRO or on a relocation's slot, an export `origin.core` lacks, a program bound against another release.

## Task S4-3: the kernel-wide bound, and O2 for step 4 (ADR-0005 Amendment 8, G2, G5 and G6; TASKS item 55; decision items 206, 209 and 210; 2026-11-13)

- **What:** every process is paid for out of the kernel's root before it is made, and the payment comes back when everything it covers is gone: task S4-3 of ADR-0011 N14 step 4 (`docs/research/2026-11-11-n14-step4-scope.md`, section 4, whose exit tests were written before the code). On `claude/elegant-benz-1983ff`, cut from `main` at `803755c` and, on the coordinating session's word, reset to `land/s4-part2` at `793299a`, which holds task S4-2. The contract and the coordinating session's rulings are TASKS item 55. No ABI, format, call or status changes. Commits:
  - `da6827f` the §78 contract; `d146b3b` the rulings that change it (the launch's own pages paid by the root, the port's index, the record tables' overestimate, the fix to `prepare_run`, the framework's read-only sizes, the V3 cost statement).
  - `46880ba` `quota.rs`: `Limits` and `MemoryLimits`, a set of limits' figure kind by kind (`footprint`, `growing`, `Costs`, `Figure`), the `Purse` and its `Payment`, the reserve, and their host tests.
  - `4595392` the definition test that holds row O2.
  - `bbc15f5` the framework's read-only sizes, in one commit as the coordinating session asked: `ObjectRef::ALLOCATION`, `userspace::{MAX_TABLES, MAX_USER_PAGES, PAGE_RECORD, SHARED_FRAME}` and `ports::{Reservation::ALLOCATIONS, Port::INDEX_SLOT, Port::FIRST_INDEX_SLOTS}`. `MAX_TABLES` was private before: one keyword in the framework, made by this task.
  - `7c7b099` a fix to S3-5b's `UserSpace::prepare_run`, found by this task, with `tablebound::ready_records` and its host tests.
  - `fbe8c34` the kernel: the payment at creation and for a launch's pages, the threads count, the root sized at boot, `HandleTable::ELEMENTS`, `Mappings::RECORD`, `ipc::channel_cost`, `sched::THREAD_STACK` made `pub(crate)`, and `threads` on every limits value in the tree.
  - `45d402a` and `16b5683` the boot proof "the kernel-wide bound", its table row and xtask's markers.
  - `8ca93c5` `rustfmt` over the task's code: the last commit that changes code.
  - the records: ADR-0013's row and controls, the two threat models, the budgets file, the matrix rows, the progress page, STATUS and this entry.
- **Specifications:** ADR-0005 P11, D4, F7, G2, G5 and G6 (G3 as a draft only); ADR-0013 R1, R6 and R7; ADR-0016 R8; ADR-0018 V3 to V5 and V8. No document outside the repository: the figure is arithmetic over the kernel's own types, and the heap's rounding and `Vec`'s growth are measured by host tests, not read from a document.
- **Open-source references consulted (§3, §6):** none. No source code of any other system was read.
- **`unsafe`:** none added or touched. The framework's three new constants are safe code in files that hold `unsafe` already; the kernel's files forbid it.
- **How the figure is measured.** Every kind's cost is the sum of the blocks the kernel allocates for one of it, each through a `size_of` and `align_of` in the build and rounded as `origin_frame::heap` rounds it (`quota::footprint`, held to the real heap's own count of bytes in use for every size to 5,000 bytes and many above, at 13 alignments). A table that grows is counted at the most it holds while it grows, its new block and its old one together (`quota::growing`, held to `Vec` as the pinned compiler builds it). As the build measured them on the development Mac: a process 134,272 bytes (its page tables at their bound, 32 frames, are most of it); a handle table of 64 entries 13,056; a channel 4,608; a memory object 64, and 80 a page besides its frame; a space's page records once it may map 2,138,240; an event 512; a port 1,024; a binding 448, eight index slots among it; a thread 21,024, its 16 KiB stack among it. A private page a launch maps costs its frame and 384 bytes of record tables.
- **Decisions this task did not take:** none of the owner's. With the coordinating session: the reserve's size, the threads count, where the payment is held, the launch's pages (changed by its ruling (d)), the growing tables, the framework's constants, the fix to `prepare_run`, and the port's index, which it put to the owner as decision item 282, accepted on 2026-11-13 as ADR-0005 Amendment 10 (I1), and built by TASKS item 57, not here.
- **Found, for other sessions:** the port's index (row K7, decision item 282); the heap's fixed slab table (row O10, TASKS item 56); `prepare_run`'s reservation before its bound (fixed here). The record tables' count is an overestimate on purpose, about 2 MiB a process that may map.
- **Limits, stated plainly:**
  - In step 4 the kernel is the only creator: the root pays for everything. A creator that is a process, paying out of its own figure, is step 5's (G3, G4).
  - A port's index is counted per binding; the slots its growth leaves after their binders' payments come back are not (K7; item 282, ADR-0005 Amendment 10, I1, TASKS item 57).
  - The heap's 1,024 slabs (4 MiB of small blocks) are a resource the root does not count (O10, TASKS item 56).
  - Frames a stalled shootdown keeps for ever, slab fragmentation, a thread object held after its thread is reaped, the concurrent growth of one port's index and undelivered messages between their refund and their reaping are each bounded otherwise, as row O11 says, and not by the root.
  - The reserve is a hypothesis (budget B19). The kernel's own use after boot is not measured.
  - No boot fills every quota of a process and compares what the kernel holds with the figure: each kind's cost rests on reading its allocations, an inventory made on 2026-11-13, and on the host tests of the heap's and `Vec`'s rules.
  - Nothing has run under KVM or on a real processor, and CI has not built this.
